articleTitle: YOLOv8-LSD: Improved YOLOv8 Focused on Small Target Information Extraction for Road Damage Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Detection of road damage is critical for improving traffic safety and extending the life of roads. Despite the enhanced accuracy offered by deep learning models such as YOLOv8 in the field of road damage detection, challenges persist due to factors like susceptibility to weather conditions and pavement composition, and the difficulty in accurately identifying and pinpointing minor damages in complex scenarios. To tackle these issues, we introduce an enhanced detection algorithm, YOLOv8-LSD. This algorithm incorporates a deformable attention mechanism and a large separable kernel attention framework, which heighten focus on key regions within the input feature map, thereby facilitating precise damage detection. Additionally, it employs spatial and channel reconstruction in the detection head to optimize convolution, ensuring meticulous feature extraction and representation. Experimental findings demonstrate that our enhanced algorithm elevates detection accuracy by 1% over the original YOLOv8 model.

articleTitle: A Semantic-Based Framework for Multi-Label Text Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: In the field of natural language processing (NLP), the objective of multi-label text categorization (MLTC) is exceedingly challenging. In order to improve multi-label text classification (MLTC) by creating associations between text and labels, many neural network (NLP) techniques have been created in the last several years. This article introduces a design for multi-label text classification (MLTC) that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs), bidirectional encoder representations of transformers (BERTs), and long short-term memory (Bi-LSTMs). First, by fine-tuning BERT for text and label data, a common vector representation with word and label embeddings is created. Next, a CNN is fed these embeddings and is tasked with extracting fine-grained features from the semantic data contained in the feature maps. Furthermore, the extracted feature maps are processed by a Bi-LSTM, whose task is to capture the inherent correlations between documents and their associated labels. Finally, to complete the classification task, a classifier is created. The thorough experimental trials indicate that our model excels past research on multiple publicly accessible datasets.

articleTitle: Text region detection algorithm for medical instruments screen based on improved DBNet
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Recognition of text in images has become increasingly important with the rapid development of cameras, and the main technology involved is Optical Character Recognition (OCR). In order to enhance the recognition accuracy of traditional text region detection algorithms for medical instrument screen data, which contains irregular and small objects, this paper introduces an improved scheme incorporating Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF) and Gaussian Error Linear Unit (GELU) activation function, and proposes the DBNeti model. The introduction of ASFF aims to address the limitations of fixed feature fusion in traditional text recognition algorithms and to enhance the performance of target detectors at different scales. The GELU is introduced as the activation function of the DBNet algorithm, utilizing its nonlinear characteristics, gradient preservation, and computational efficiency to enhance the expressiveness and generalization ability of the model. Experiments demonstrate that the improved model, DBNeti, has achieved optimal performance across all evaluation indices, including an Accuracy of 0.8189, a Recall of 0.3633, a Precision of 0.6858, and an F-measure of 0.4750. Compared to DBNet, DBNeti improves the Accuracy, Recall, Precision, and F-measure indices by 3.3%, 6.1%, 3.1%, and 4.2%, respectively. This study demonstrates the superiority of the DBNeti algorithm in the text recognition task.

articleTitle: An efficient multimodal imaging device for acquiring high quality dorsal hand vein and finger vein images based on adaptive dimming
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: It is attractive to collect multimodal information of same subject simultaneously for high-performance biometrics, comparing with biometric techniques based on single modality. In this study, we develop a multimodal vein acquisition device which can capture infrared images of finger veins (FV) and dorsal hand veins (DHV) at the same time. The device has two specific characteristics. First, it adopts a novel structural design that facilitates flexible assembly of light source boards. Second, a simple and efficient dimming algorithm based on U-Net was proposed to adapt to complex environments e.g. unbalanced illumination, different hand thicknesses, etc. The quality of two kinds of vein images collected by the device are evaluated, and comparisons are made to confirm the superiority of collecting multi-modalities vein images simultaneously for personal identification. The developed device is believed to play promising role in multimodal biometrics.

articleTitle: Dental Arch Curve Optimization from Standard Dental Arch Curves
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Cone Beam Computed Tomography serves as a crucial imaging modality in oral diagnostics and treatment planning. This study presents an innovative method for detecting dental arch curves from CBCT datasets by optimizing a standard form. The proposed method first generates an axial maximum intensity projection image from slices with tooth crowns for separating teeth and jaw bones. Next, a standard dental arch form is set and optimized using an energy function. The reconstructed panoramic image based on the detected dental arch more accurately represents the maxillofacial structures, even when affected by metal artifacts.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale CNN with Graph-Convolutional Classifier for Classification of Hyperspectral Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Hyperspectral image(HSI) classification is one of the core technologies in remote sensing that has attracted a great deal of attention. In recent years, with the application of deep learning methods such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), graph convolutional neural networks (GCNs), and vision-transformers in this field, the accuracy of HSI classification has been pushed to a new stage. However, these models use some downsampling blocks to compress the sampling zone into a feature vector, which is then fed directly into the classifier. This model structure results in the feature vector containing information about all pixels in the sampling zone, which may interfere with the classification results of the classifier. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a novel multi-scale CNN with graph-convolutional classifier (MSCGC) for HSI classification, which exploits feature vector space reconstruction and uses graph convolution as the space information transfer to build a quality feature vector. The multi-scale fusion process enables the backbone to retain a greater quantity of spatial information within the feature vector, thus allowing for the restoration of the spatial structure through the application of bilinear interpolation. The feature vectors are capable of achieving a one-to-one mapping with the original hyperspectral image at the spatial scale. The graph convolution head is capable of automatically learning the spatial relationship between the center vector and surrounding vectors, thereby efficiently using the feature vectors provided by the backbone to accurately classify HSI. Experimental results on the two hyperspectral datasets validated the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Fruit and Vegetable Recognition Method based on AugMSR-CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: The traditional manual settlement method is characterized by low efficiency, high labor and resource consumption, and significant negative impact on consumers' shopping experience. To effectively address the aforementioned issues, a fruit and vegetable recognition model based on the MSR-CNN algorithm is proposed in this paper. Additionally, an AugFPN feature pyramid is innovatively incorporated into the MSR-CNN algorithm to enhance the model's generalization ability. Experimental results demonstrate that the model, based on the algorithm proposed in this paper, achieves an average increase of 1.4 percentage points in AP value, greatly improving the recognition rate of fruits and vegetables.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimization Method of Electric Power Construction Schedule Based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: With the rapid development of the economy and technology, the demand for electricity is rising, so the construction of electricity is increasing year by year. Therefore, the importance of power construction progress management in power construction is also increasing. In order to effectively improve the construction progress in power construction, a power construction progress optimization method based on the BP neural network is proposed. Based on three-dimensional model simulation, the accuracy of construction progress estimation is improved by comparing the simulation progress with the actual construction progress. Firstly, a genetic algorithm is used to establish a 3D model to simulate the progress of the electric power construction site, and the obtained model is bound to the actual construction tasks. Secondly, the electric power construction progress library is established, and the weight of progress evaluation indexes is adjusted. Then, the neural network is used to evaluate the progress of power construction so as to provide early warning for the existence of progress risk. Finally, the proposed optimization method is applied to a specific construction site by using a case study method. The results show that using this method, the success rate of early warning of construction progress is 99.68%.

articleTitle: Research on Bolt Loosening Fault Detection Method in Random Vibration Test Based on Acoustic Event Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: In the course of aerospace product development tests, loose bolt failures can significantly compromise the effectiveness of durability vibration assessments, leading to potential damage to components and even posing risks of personnel injuries. To addressing the above issue, a real-time intelligent detection method for bolt loosening fault based on Deep Learning is proposed. This approach aims to promptly and accurately identify instances of the loose bolt fault. The diagnostic dataset for bolt loosening fault is generated by collecting audio signals from random vibration test scenarios by using microphones, and the audio signals are then separately transformed into Log Mel spectrogram image and MFCC spectrogram image, serving as inputs for the construction and training of two Convolutional Neural Network model, respectively. The Deep Convolutional Neural Network model (VGG16) is also applied. These models are trained to discern whether the collected audio indicates a loose bolt fault. Experimental results reveal that, in comparison to the Log Mel spectrogram image, the use of MFCC spectrogram image as network inputs enhances detection accuracy by 5.62%, the fault detection speed of the CNN model surpasses that of the VGG16 network, achieving real-time monitoring capabilities with a speed of 161ms, this validates the proposed method's real-time and effective performance in detecting loose bolt fault during random vibration experiment, thereby the application of Deep Learning is advanced in the field of bolt loosening fault detection.

articleTitle: Infrared Ship Object Detection Utilizing Deformable Large Kernel Convolution and a Highly Sensitive Intersection over Union Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Infrared object detection, due to its unique ability to penetrate clouds and fog, can be well used for ship object detection tasks. However, the application of existing object detection algorithms may be challenged significantly by the low resolution of infrared images. To address this issue, we have proposed a method that comprises two key components. Firstly, we introduced a spatial pyramid pooling module based on deformable large kernel convolution (SPP-DLC), which enhances the model's discriminatory ability between infrared objects and the background by expanding the receptive field of the convolution kernel. Secondly, we designed the Expand-IoU, a highly sensitive Intersection over Union (IoU) loss that accelerates the convergence process by incorporating large-scale auxiliary boxes and leveraging the length and width information of the bounding boxes. In addition, we filmed and produced an infrared ship target (SPT) dataset for ship object detection tasks due to the lack of public datasets. Based on the SPT dataset, we conducted a series of comparison experiments. Experiments show that our proposed module and loss function can enhance the network's detection capability, thereby making our approach superior to other comparison algorithms. Compared with the basic method, the algorithm with the SPP-DLC module and Expand-IoU improved by 8.4% on mAP50.

articleTitle: Enhanced Tile Defect Detection with Optimized Cascade R-CNN for Efficient Quality Control
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: With the need for high-speed production in the ceramic tile manufacturing industry, automated quality control becomes critical for enhancing efficiency and reducing costs. Addressing this urgent demand, we have devised a new detection method based on Cascade R-CNN. We improved the model's structure and training methods to match the needs of tile defect detection. Regarding the architecture, we chose ResNeSt as the backbone to enhance feature extraction capabilities, introduced DCN to increase the model's adaptability to target shapes, and integrated a recursive feature pyramid to improve the model's extraction of multi-scale features. In terms of training strategies, we implemented data augmentation and multi-scale training/testing to improve the model's generalization ability and robustness. In addition, online hard example mining was applied during training to address the imbalance between positive and negative samples. Finally, we proved the improvements' effectiveness through ablation and comparative experiments. Compared to Cascade R-CNN, we achieved a 9.0% improvement in mAP, providing reliable and efficient technical support for quality control in the tile manufacturing industry.

articleTitle: Global Contextual Learning Network for Multisource Remote Sensing Image Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Multisource remote sensing image fusion aims to combine the complementary advantage of different modalities for fine-grained classification. Current multisource image fusion methods are based on a patch-by-patch learning paradigm, which requires high computational burden. In addition, how to combine different attributes is still a challenging issue. In this article, a global contextual learning network (GCLNet) is studied for multisource remote sensing image fusion. In GCLNet, an encoder-decoder convolutional network is proposed to draw global spectral-spatial information, which can significantly reduce the computing cost. Furthermore, a contextual attention feature fusion module is designed to connect coarse-to-fine features between encoder and decoder. Experiments on Augsburg and Yellow River datasets reveal that the proposed GCLNet obtains promising results in the light of classification result and inference speed compared to other advanced fusion methods.

articleTitle: Comparison and Analysis of Coral Reef Substrate Classification Methods Using Underwater Optical Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: To explore the spatial distribution of substrate types using underwater optical data from coral reefs, this study utilizes field survey data from the coral reef ecosystem around Jiajing Island, Hainan Province, collected on June 20, 2022. A classification system for coral reef substrate types was developed, and various methods, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE), Neural Networks (NN), Minimum Distance Method (MD), Spectral Information Divergence (SID), ISODATA, and K-MEANS, were employed to conduct experiments on underwater coral reef substrate classification. The results indicate that SVM performs best in underwater coral reef substrate classification, with the highest accuracy and Kappa coefficient of 66.28% and 0.52, respectively. Clump clustering post-processing improves the overall accuracy of the classification method, and in particular, RF and NN have significant improvement, which is slightly lower than that of SVM but remains above 60%.

articleTitle: Residual Dual Attention Generative Adversarial Networks for Tissue Segmentation on Histopathological Image
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Breast cancer is a common malignant tumor among women, posing a significant threat to their health. Pathological images are considered the standard for breast cancer detection and diagnosis, where the epithelial tissue and stromal tissue within them play a crucial role in the tumor microenvironment. However, accurate segmentation of epithelial tissue and stromal tissue in breast cancer pathological images is challenging due to their complex structures and high-density data. Despite the impressive performance of deep learning methods, they only focus on pixel level, neglecting the high-order consistency of the images. Therefore, we proposed a residual dual attention generative adversarial network model for breast cancer pathological image segmentation, called RDAGAN. The RDAGAN incorporates the generative adversarial networks and adopts dual attention mechanisms to capture visual feature dependencies in both spatial and channel dimensions. It ensures overall structural consistency in the segmentation results. We evaluated our method on two datasets, i.e., the NKI and VGH, and achieved promising performance than the comparing methods.

articleTitle: Error Evaluation Analysis of Electricity Metering Device Based on Transformer Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Aiming at the current problem of not being able to assess the error of power metering device in real time, an error assessment algorithm for power metering devices based on the characteristics of the transformer is proposed. The method is based on the principal element analysis of the root mean square (RMS) value of the secondary signal of the transformer, and establishes a multi-parameter model of the error of the power metering device under the normal metering condition, and uses the support vector machine regression algorithm to obtain the metering error of the transformer under the actual working condition. By synthesizing the secondary circuit error and the power meter error with the metering error under the actual working condition of the transformer, the synthesized error can be obtained. The method can be used in real-time monitoring for state evaluation of power metering errors and real-time assessment of errors. Simulation verification shows that the method has high accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Bad Data Detection in Power Grid Based on Improved Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Based on the improved gap statistical algorithm, the bad data of the power system is mined so as to accomplish the detection and identification of bad data of power system, and improve the accuracy and effectiveness of detection. Taking the real-time data of the actual power grid as the basic data and test data, the algorithm program is written and simulation analysis is carried out to verify the correctness of the algorithm by considering a variety of cases containing bad data.

articleTitle: Multi-Site Federated Brain Disease Diagnosis Method Based on Brain Topology Prototypes
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: The multi-site analysis provides the potential for improving diagnostic accuracy by integrating data from various sites. However, despite its above promise, multi-site applications face challenges such as data leakage and the non-independence and non-identical distribution of data. In this paper, we propose a method for multi-site joint brain disease diagnosis using brain network topological prototypes. Leveraging the federated learning (FL) framework, our approach enables collaborative analysis of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data across multiple sites without sharing raw data, thus ensuring data privacy. By fusing brain networks constructed from multi-site topology prototypes with local Pearson coefficients, we develop a contrastive learning-based model for brain disease diagnosis capable of identifying brain diseases and extracting topological structure prototypes. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing federated learning algorithms on multi-site datasets related to Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD).

articleTitle: RKTrans: Transformer with Improved Residual Connection Units for Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Existing Transformer-based time series forecasting models fail to balance the requirements of power forecasting, including long-range dependencies capture, real-time forecasting, and retention of sequential information simultaneously. To address this issue, we propose RKTrans, a Transformer-based forecasting model that associates the residual network in the Transformer with Euler discretization of solutions to Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE) and replaces classic residual units with the Runge-Kutta block for accurate and real-time forecasting. Our research provides insights for effectively applying Transformer models to power forecasting. Furthermore, RKTrans surpasses existing state-of-the-art Transformer models on public datasets with less inference time. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/KongMLin/RKTrans.

articleTitle: TASGCN: A Temporal Attention and Spatial Graph Convolution Network for Multivariate Time Series Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Multivariate time series prediction is extremely important but challenging in fields such as finance, energy, transportation, etc. Due to the highly complex dependencies between pairs of variables and the non-stationarity of time series, existing works fail to obtain satisfactory results. We are committed to modeling complex spatial-temporal relationships in multivariate time series, proposing TASGCN, which adapts the attention mechanism to extract temporal relations and graph convolution to model spatial dependencies. Specifically we introduce a graph generation layer to dynamically extract directed relations among variables. TASGCN demonstrates excellent prediction results in our datasets originating from real-world data from data center computer room environments. In particular, TASGCN outperforms other advanced baseline models by up to 26% in terms of the MAE evaluation metric.

articleTitle: Sand-Dust Image Enhancement Algorithm Based on Lab Space
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: To address the issues of color shift, low sharpness, and low contrast in dust images, this paper proposes an improvement algorithm rooted in Lab space. This method leverages the separation of color and brightness in Lab space for correction and enhancement. Initially, color shift in dust images is corrected in the a and b channels. Next, detail and contrast are improved in the L channel through Laplacian sharpening and contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization. Adaptive gamma correction is subsequently employed on enhance brightness. Finally, the images are converted back to RGB color space, and histogram stretching is performed, resulting in clear dust images. Experiments show that the proposed method effectively resolves color shift issues and enhances image clarity and detail.

articleTitle: Research on Small Target Detection and Recognition Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8 for Aerial Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) encounter various challenges in flight and imaging in everyday scenarios. These challenges include the limited representation of ground objects in UAV-captured images, the dense distribution of ground objects, and the characteristics of small targets such as their small size, high speed, and maneuverability. These factors often result in small pixel points in images, making it challenging to accurately detect them using existing UAV detection methods. The study introduces a novel dynamic head framework, named Dynamic Head (DyHead), which integrates target detection head and attention mechanisms to emphasize the fusion of shallow features for efficient information interaction and fusion. Furthermore, the study enhances the feature weights of dense small targets and incorporates a multi-branch fusion module called Diverse Branch Block (DBB) in C2f to enhance the feature extraction capability of small objects. In the experiment of the VisDrone2019 dataset, the enhanced PDD-YOLOv8 model demonstrates significant performance improvements compared to the standardized YOLOv8s model without increasing parameters. Notably, the mean average precision (mAP) increases by 8.5 and 5.9 percentage points at IoU thresholds of 0.5 and 0.5:0.95, respectively, demonstrating strong specificity and performance.

articleTitle: Research on Data Acquisition Method of Power System Based on Compressed Sensing Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of large amounts of data and difficult transmission and storage in the process of power system data acquisition, a new power system data acquisition method based on the compressed sensing principle is proposed. The method uses the compressed sensing principle to sparse the original data, and then uses greedy algorithm to reconstruct the original data through a small amount of data, which greatly reduces the hardware burden of data signal acquisition in a power system. Simulink was used to build a new power grid data acquisition system. A random demodulator was used in the sampling module and OMP algorithm was used in the data reconstruction module. Experimental results show that the new system can still effectively reconstruct the original data at a small sampling rate and has good anti-interference ability.

articleTitle: A CNN-based Airborne Weather Risk Warning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: In this study, A CNN-based airborne weather risk warning method is proposed. This method can autonomously predict weather risk according to airborne weather radar data during flight. We use CNN to construct a weather risk prediction model, and convert airborne weather radar data into RGB images for risk identification. The model can provide weather risk warning when the pilots are distracted or have a heavy workload, and it has the advantages of high reliability, high efficiency, little computing power requirement, and can be stably run on the airborne deep learning inference platform. We perform the experiment using a Airbus A321 airplane model in a flight simulator, and the experiment results show that the weather risk prediction model can quickly and accurately identify weather risks, with an accuracy of 97.5%. We analyze the cases of misidentification and find that most of the cases belong to the middle state between risk and no risk.

articleTitle: Uncertainty-Aware Prototype Learning for Open-Set Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Hyperspectral image classification, aiming to assign an unique label for each pixel, has garnered much more attention in recent years. However, current most classification approaches assume that all classes between training and test sets are consistent, which limits their applications for identifying the unknowns. In this article, an uncertainty-aware prototype learning model (UAPLM) is proposed for open-set hyperspectral image classification. First, a spectral-spatial convolutional network is utilized to extract the high-order semantic information from input data. Then, feature consistency and sample uncertainty are estimated to obtain the probability of an unknown class. Finally, the known class probabilities obtained by the fully connected layer and the unknown class probabilities are integrated to yield the final classification result. Experiments on several datasets demonstrate that the proposed UAPLM can better recognize the known and unknown samples compared to other open-set classification methods.

articleTitle: A flexible and Comprehensive Approach for Assessing Cooperative Intelligence Levels of Unmanned Swarms
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: This paper presents a flexible and complex approach for assessing the cooperative intelligence grades of unmanned system swarms by improving and integrating the classic observe-orient-decide-act (OODA) ring, the traditional analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and fuzzy complex evaluation (FCE) method. The established assessment indicator system can more complexly and properly reflect their intrinsic cooperative intelligence realization in some complex scenarios. The improved assessment approach can more flexibly and objectively obtain the weight values of various assessment factors and the overall cooperative intelligence grades of unmanned system swarms because of the integration of extension theory, fuzzy technology, and collective decision-making thinking. Both theoretical analyses and experimental results show that the approach is more flexible, objective, and practical than previous approaches.

articleTitle: Multi-View Graph Attention Complementary based Brain Networks Analysis for Brain Diseases Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: The integration of functional and structural imaging data significantly enhances the analysis of brain networks, which is essential for diagnosing brain disorders. Existing methods primarily focus on merging feature spaces across modalities. However, vector-based approaches do not preserve the topology of the brain network, while traditional graph-based methods limit information aggregation, thereby impeding the effective extraction of complementary information and topological features. In our research, we introduce an innovative approach by combining functional magnetic resonance Imaging (fMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) techniques to diagnose epilepsy. Our framework intelligently combines diverse brain network aggregation methods to capture complementary topological features. Initially, we construct multimodal brain networks and employ multi-channel graph neural networks to extract topological features. Secondly, we integrate an attention-based system to merge feature embeddings from different brain networks dynamically and craft a loss function to highlight the prominent features among different aggregation approaches. Finally, we classify the integrated features using a multi-layer perceptron (MLP). Experimental evaluation of an epilepsy dataset from Jinling Hospital demonstrates a significant improvement in diagnosis performance compared to several advanced diagnostic methods.

articleTitle: Global Scanpath Encoder: A Transformer-Based Learning Model to Identify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Unlike visual attention modeling to predict commonalities among different subjects, using eye movements for group recognition, such as distinguishing children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), has been a challenging task. In recent years, various machine learning-based ASD recognition models have emerged to provide an objective mode to assist in ASD screening. However, existing classification models mainly rely on static saliency maps and don’t utilize the global semantic information of each fixation, which cannot reconstruct the critical semantic perception in the actual attention. To address this issue, we propose a Global Scanpath Encoder (GSE) based eye movement classification model. Based on the coupled scanpaths and images, we train a ViT network to extract global features for each fixation. Additionally, we implicitly encode the order information of fixations on each scanpath for the final SVM-based classification. In the experiment, we recorded the data of 28 children with ASD and 30 typically developing (TD) children on 220 stimuli. The experimental results showed that the proposed model outperforms the state-of-the-art eye-tracking-based ASD recognition models, significantly improving the accuracy of identifying ASD samples. Additionally, our model has robust scalability, and the features encoded by the model can be applied to various downstream analyses, advancing research on other eye-tracking-based tasks.

articleTitle: 3D Human Animation Synthesis based on a Temporal Diffusion Generative Model
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Three-dimensional human motion generation is an important branch of computer graphics and has broad application prospects. Traditional human animation synthesis technologies rely on professional simulation platforms with high labor and time costs. Existing learning-based methods usually generate human animations by giving the prior motion seed, which lacks generative ability and cannot generate a wide variety of human motions. On the other hand, established generative methods rely on a given prior sample distribution, and their creation capabilities are relatively limited. To that end, we propose a distribution-free human motion synthesis workflow based on a temporal diffusion model. By specifying the high-level semantic motion info, our method is able to generate a wide variety of human motions with diverse styles. Firstly, we construct our human motion dataset by selecting the human motion sequences that cover different motion types and labeling them with the corresponding motion semantics. Secondly, we use the temporal network Transformer to extract the motion semantic features of different kinds of human motion sequences and introduce the self-attention mechanism to ensure temporal continuity between adjacent motion frames. Then, we use the diffusion model to denoise the extracted motion semantic features to generate visually continuous, realistic, and delicate motion sequences. Finally, we conduct a series of experiments on HumanAct12 and UESTC datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves better performance in motion reconstruction and generation, and has greater improvements on a few metrics including RMSE, STED, FID, diversity, etc.

articleTitle: Eye Movement Classification and Prediction via Attention-Based Distribution Distance
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Intelligent Algorithms (PRMVIA)
abstract: Eye-tracking classification often relies on the training of deep neural networks. Despite good performance, the interpretability of the hidden output of the classification networks is unclear, making the representation learning and regularization challenging. In this study, we propose a simple but effective eye movement classification model to identify children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) based on Attention-Based Distribution Distance (ABDD). We first explore a Reference Attention-Based Distribution in each image from the actual eye movement data. Then, we utilize the difference in eye movement distribution between the ASD group and the typically developing (TD) group to assign higher weights for the images. Finally, we estimate the classification threshold by fitting a Weibull distribution and achieve subject-wise classification. In eye movement classification tasks, we can take the statistic as a teacher model to pre-train neural networks as a student model, enabling them to converge quickly. Furthermore, we know that the hidden layer output of the neural network is related to the attention distribution on the image. The experiment confirmed that the proposed method can achieve results comparable to deep models and assist in pretraining of Eye-tracking classification tasks.
